issue-53-crowding.broke: The gutter between two columns was a constant 132px and a tag was as wide as its text, so a 235px pill was drawn clipped behind the next column's boxes. Node boxes reached 300px because a `sub` that was a sentence never wrapped.
issue-53-crowding.fixed: Each boundary is now as wide as the widest tag crossing it, and node text and tag pills both wrap.

issue-52-fan-out.broke: Two things at once. The labels of a fan-out landed on the wrong lines — the board read as if Worker parked into Postgres — and the edge closing the loop left the DLQ through its own name, which rendered as `D|Q`.
issue-52-fan-out.fixed: The gutter work for #53 gave the fan-out tags their own lines. The loop's anchor and floor now clear the strip a queue keeps its name in.

issue-58-boundary-members.broke: A boundary was drawn as the bounding box of its members, so when the members were not adjacent in the layout the dashed enclosure also took in every box between them. `NOT A MEMBER` was drawn inside a box labelled `MEMBERS: A AND D ONLY`, and `NOT A MEMBER EITHER` stayed outside only because it happened to fall below the rectangle. #52 part 3 is the same bug, where `b` sits between `a` and `c` in the flow and no column assignment can make them adjacent.
issue-58-boundary-members.fixed: Columns are still the flow's, but a box inside a boundary's columns that is not a member is now stood wholly above or wholly below the enclosure, so the rectangle is true by construction. A boundary that two others make impossible is drawn as the smallest set of true pieces instead of one false rectangle.
